channel.title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - All Critical Infrastructure
channel.description: Curated OT/ICS advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] A third Citrix NetScaler zero-day is exploited, and a fourth critical flaw was patched on 9 October
item.description: Citrix has confirmed a third NetScaler zero-day under attack, days after patching two others that were exploited for weeks before disclosure, and on 9 October it shipped a fourth fix. The exploited trio is CVE-2026-88771, CVE-2026-88772 and CVE-2026-88779 (a SAML-only memory overflow, CVSS v4 8.7); the federal KEV deadline for the newest passed on 7 October. The earlier pair brought web shells, rogue admin accounts and configuration theft, and patching does not evict an intruder. The new CVE-2026-107406 (CVSS 9.5) is another SAML memory overflow that Citrix says could allow code execution; no exploitation is reported, but it affects builds through 14.1-73.41 and 13.1-64.28, so appliances patched last week need yet another upgrade. NetScaler often fronts remote access into plant networks, making an unhunted appliance a possible foothold toward OT. - Citrix security bulletins CTX697096 and CTX697174 (and the 9 Oct bulletin for CVE-2026-107406); CISA KEV catalog; Dutch NCSC; Tenable, watchTowr, LevelBlue, Arctic Wolf and Mandiant/GTIG research; reported by SecurityWeek, BleepingComputer, The Hacker News, Cybersecurity Dive and Help Net Security - Fourth flaw CVE-2026-107406 patched 9 Oct 2026, no exploitation reported (The Hacker News, 9 Oct); CVE-2026-88779 fixed 3–4 Oct and added to KEV 4 Oct 2026 (deadline 7 Oct, now passed); watchTowr denial-of-service finding and CISA/Australian warnings 5 Oct 2026 (SecurityWeek and The Record, 5 Oct); first two flaws confirmed and patched 27 Sep 2026, mass exploitation after a 28 Sep proof-of-concept write-up; post-exploitation analysis 1 Oct 2026

item.title: [Critical] Colorado confirms foreign hackers altered pumps and disabled alarms at two small water systems
item.category: Incident — confirmed foreign intrusion into two small, privately owned drinking-water systems; pumping cycles and alarms altered; no known impact to treatment or public safety; actors unidentified; no new development since disclosure
item.description: Colorado Governor Jared Polis’s office confirmed on 18 September that foreign cyber actors breached two small, privately owned water systems in late August, changing equipment settings, disabling remote access and alarms, and altering pumping cycles. Officials describe the disruption as brief, with no known impact to treatment, water quality or public safety, and say they cannot yet confirm which foreign actors were responsible. A separately tracked, broader Iran-linked campaign against US water systems has not been formally connected to this incident. It remains the only confirmed case of OT tampering in this edition, with nothing new reported since the initial disclosure. - Colorado Governor’s office statement (18 Sep 2026), reported by Axios Denver and Industrial Cyber (22 Sep) - Intrusions late Aug 2026; confirmed 18 Sep 2026 — no new development as of this edition

item.title: [High] Hackers reached a US-bound tanker’s propulsion system, Bloomberg reports; the FBI says there was no disruption
item.category: Incident — Bloomberg reports, citing unnamed US officials, that hackers temporarily reached the propulsion system of the US-bound tanker VL Prosperity; FBI on record: no operational disruption, instability or crew danger; actor, duration and extent of control unknown; a second tanker was boarded in the Gulf of Mexico
item.description: Bloomberg reported on 2 October, citing US officials who asked not to be named, that FBI and Coast Guard investigators found hackers had temporarily accessed the propulsion system of the very large crude carrier VL Prosperity as it approached the Texas coast this summer. Neither agency has confirmed that finding on the record. The FBI’s on-record statement says there are no reports of operational disruption, vessel instability, danger to crews or environmental impact, and Bloomberg says it is unclear how long the access lasted or what the intruders could control. No one has been publicly blamed. VL Prosperity was boarded in the Atlantic on 21 August after it lost communications, and a second, unnamed tanker was boarded in the Gulf of Mexico days later. Earlier engine-room manipulation claims from Iranian media remain unverified. - Bloomberg (citing unnamed US officials), via Supply Chain Brain and gCaptain; FBI statement; boarding details per the US Coast Guard, Dragos and Reuters - Boardings 21 and 24 Aug 2026; propulsion-system access reported 2 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] FBI and Secret Service say the FortiBleed campaign against Fortinet VPN gateways is still running
item.category: Incident — FBI and Secret Service re-warn that the “FortiBleed” credential-harvesting campaign against internet-facing Fortinet FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways remains active; reused or leaked credentials, no CVE; no OT victim named
item.description: The FBI and US Secret Service warned on 7 October that attackers are still scanning internet-facing FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways with credentials harvested earlier in the campaign. First documented in June, it had collected more than 86,000 working device credentials across 194 countries by 19 June, according to The Hacker News. No vulnerability is involved: the attackers rely on reused or leaked passwords, interception of login traffic and cracking of weakly stored hashes. Some victims were locked out when attackers created new admin accounts, then deleted or reset the legitimate ones; the FBI also says the chain has served as an entry point for ransomware affiliates, and SOCRadar’s latest count is 86,644 compromised devices. Researchers describe a Russian-speaking operator that may be selling access, with overlaps to INC and Lynx ransomware; that attribution is reported, not confirmed. Fortinet gateways often sit at the IT/OT boundary. - FBI and US Secret Service warning, reported by The Hacker News, BleepingComputer and The Record; CISA mitigation guidance (June 2026) - Ongoing — re-warned 7 Oct 2026; SecurityWeek follow-up on admin lockouts 8 Oct 2026; campaign first documented June 2026

item.title: [Medium] Southern Company notifies about 400,000 Georgia Power and Alabama Power customers of a portal data breach
item.category: Incident — IT-side breach at a major US utility holding company; customer-portal data accessed; no OT or grid impact reported; actor not named
item.description: Southern Company says an unauthorized third party reached customer information through its online customer portal and that it is notifying roughly 400,000 customers, about 300,000 at Georgia Power and 100,000 at Alabama Power, with Mississippi Power also named in the notice. Exposed data includes names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses and the last four digits of Social Security numbers; the company says bank account, payment card and driver’s licence numbers were not accessed. It has engaged law enforcement and offered a year of credit monitoring. No effect on grid or plant operations has been reported, and the method of access has not been disclosed. For OT teams the relevance is indirect: customer-facing web portals are an IT-side exposure, and the case is a reminder to confirm that nothing on those systems has a path into operations networks. - Southern Company public notice, reported by SecurityWeek - Reported 7 Oct 2026

item.title: [Medium] FBI takes down domains behind Flax Typhoon’s scanning and phishing tools used against energy and airport targets
item.category: Threat Intelligence — FBI seizes seven domains behind the MicroScan and FishHub tooling of China-linked Flax Typhoon; joint FBI, CISA, NSA advisory lists power, gas and airport targets; no OT compromise confirmed
item.description: On 8 October the FBI announced it had seized seven domains used to run two hacking tools, MicroScan and FishHub, attributed to the China-linked group tracked as Flax Typhoon (also Ethereal Panda). MicroScan is a Python scanner with more than 1,300 testing scripts, used alongside a Mirai botnet; FishHub handles spear-phishing, malware delivery and data theft. A joint FBI, CISA and NSA advisory with international partners lists targets that include a South Carolina power company, airports in Japan and Poland, and Taiwanese gas and electricity firms, though the FBI did not confirm those were breached. Confirmed compromises are limited to Taiwanese universities. The advisory names older vulnerabilities such as CVE-2019-11510 (Pulse Secure VPN) and CVE-2021-22205 (GitLab). Authorities tie the actor to China-based Integrity Technology Group; they note not all activity may be linked to it. No operational-technology intrusion is described. - FBI action and joint FBI/CISA/NSA advisory, reported by BleepingComputer and The Hacker News - Announced 8 Oct 2026

item.title: [Medium] Russia-aligned UAC-0099 keeps reworking its MatchBoil downloader against Ukrainian transport and energy firms
item.category: Threat Intelligence — ESET research (reported 8 Oct 2026) on MatchBoil, a downloader used by the Russia-aligned UAC-0099 group against Ukrainian transport, manufacturing and energy firms; observed infections are in Ukraine only; no OT impact described
item.description: ESET has published new research on MatchBoil, a downloader used by the espionage group UAC-0099, which ESET assesses is likely working in Russia’s interests. The tool collects system details, pulls further malware from an attacker server and sets up persistence, and arrives mainly through phishing links. ESET saw infections at several transport companies in mid-2025, a manufacturer in December 2025 and an energy company in June 2026, all in Ukraine, and finds the code has been under development since at least July 2024, with a version seen as recently as April 2026. Earlier CERT-UA reporting tied it to fake court-summons lures that delivered a backdoor and an information stealer. The activity is IT-side espionage rather than control-system tampering, but it shows sustained interest in infrastructure operators. - ESET research, with earlier CERT-UA reporting; reported by The Record - Reported 8 Oct 2026

item.title: [Info] Claroty survey: most operators had an attack hit operations last year, and third-party access is the common thread
item.category: Research — Claroty survey of 2,000 business and technology leaders in 16 industries: 58% say a cyberattack affected operations in the past year; three-quarters link an incident to third-party access; survey self-reporting, not incident data
item.description: Claroty’s “Global State of Operational Security 2026” reports that 58% of respondents had a cyberattack affect their operational environments over the past 12 months, with downtime (43%) and safety incidents (40%) the most cited impacts. The average loss was about $1.04 million and the average outage three days. Seventy-five percent had at least one operations-affecting incident tied to third-party access, yet 49% monitor those connections only partly or not at all, and only 16% say IT and OT security are fully integrated. A separate Rockwell Automation survey reported the same day found 46% of industrial organizations had a cyber incident in the past year. Both are vendor-commissioned self-reports, useful for budgeting arguments rather than as measured attack counts. - Claroty “Global State of Operational Security 2026” and Rockwell Automation “Operational Resilience in the Age of Connectivity”, reported by Industrial Cyber - Reported 8 Oct 2026

item.title: [Critical] Chained flaws in an IO-Link master hand an unauthenticated attacker root — and a say over sensor data
item.category: Research — CERT@VDE advisory VDE-2026-014: 18 CVEs across Pepperl+Fuchs ICE2/ICE3 IO-Link masters, including a CVSS 9.8 authentication bypass and a persistent command-injection flaw; chainable for unauthenticated root; fixed firmware available; no known exploitation
item.description: CERT@VDE disclosed 18 vulnerabilities in Pepperl+Fuchs’s ICE2 and ICE3 series IO-Link masters on 16 September in advisory VDE-2026-014. The worst, CVE-2026-27546, is an authentication bypass scored CVSS 9.8; a companion flaw, CVE-2026-27565, lets an attacker inject operating-system commands through a malicious IODD file upload that persists after reboot. Chained together, they give an unauthenticated attacker root on the device and the ability to manipulate the sensor and actuator data passing through it. Nozomi Networks’ 29 September write-up counts 19 flaws in the ICE2 model and says two HTTPS requests are enough to take root. These devices bridge field sensors to the controller, a layer many OT monitoring programs don’t cover. - CERT@VDE advisory VDE-2026-014 - Published 16 Sep 2026; Nozomi technical write-up 29 Sep 2026

item.title: [High] CVSS 10.0 flaws in Toptech’s terminal-management software lead CISA’s 29 September ICS batch
item.category: Advisory — CISA ICS batch of 29 Sep 2026 (ICSA-26-272-01 to -07), led by Toptech TMS7/TopHAT 7.6.3 (CVE-2026-71379, CVSS 10.0); also Lantronix G520 cellular gateways, VIVOTEK cameras (CVSS 10.0, public proof-of-concept) and MikroTik RouterOS CVE-2026-84411; no known exploitation
item.description: CISA released seven ICS advisories on 29 September. The most serious for operators is ICSA-26-272-02: ten flaws in Toptech Systems’ TMS7 and TopHAT 7.6.3, software used to run fuel and bulk-liquid terminals (our description; CISA lists the energy, chemical and transportation sectors). The worst, CVE-2026-71379, exposes files to outside parties and scores CVSS 10.0; others include an unrestricted file upload (9.1) and five SQL injections (9.0), which CISA says could let an attacker reach critical data or run code. Release 7.8 fixes them, and Toptech notified customers in July. The batch also covers Lantronix G520 cellular gateways (fixed in 2.6.0.7R6; CISA lists water, energy and transportation), a VIVOTEK camera command-injection flaw (CVSS 10.0) with public proof-of-concept code, and MikroTik RouterOS CVE-2026-84411 (CVSS 9.8, fixed in 7.24), which is not in KEV. Baicells, Anjvision and Viidure products in the batch have no fix planned. CISA reports no known exploitation of any of them. - CISA ICS advisories ICSA-26-272-01 to -07 - Released 29 Sep 2026; Toptech customer advisory 20 Jul 2026

item.title: [Critical] Check Point’s federal patch deadline has passed for two exploited flaws spanning the VPN gateway and the server that manages it
item.category: Advisory — CVE-2026-85102 (Security Gateway/Spark VPN, certificate validation) and CVE-2026-93616 (management servers/SmartEvent, path traversal), Check Point; both exploited in the wild; added to CISA KEV 22 Sep 2026, federal deadline 25 Sep 2026 now passed
item.description: Check Point has confirmed exploitation of two separate flaws now past their federal remediation deadline. CVE-2026-85102, an improper certificate-validation issue on Security Gateways and Spark firewalls running site-to-site or remote-access VPN, allows unauthenticated remote code execution. CVE-2026-93616, a pre-authentication path traversal affecting Security Management Server, Multi-Domain Security Management, Log Servers and SmartEvent, lets an unauthenticated attacker upload and run scripts. CISA added both to KEV on 22 September alongside flaws in Arista VeloCloud and F5 BIG-IP APM; the 25 September deadline has now passed. Check Point gateways commonly sit at the IT/OT boundary and at small, unmanned sites. - Check Point security advisory; CISA KEV catalog; reported by BleepingComputer and Help Net Security - Exploitation confirmed by 22 Sep 2026; KEV addition 22 Sep 2026; federal deadline 25 Sep 2026, now passed

item.title: [High] Cisco warns of a fifth SD-WAN zero-day this year: an authentication bypass in SD-WAN Manager is being exploited
item.category: Advisory — Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager authentication-bypass zero-day (CVE-2026-76504, Cisco CVSS 9.8) exploited in the wild; fixed releases available; added to CISA KEV 30 Sep 2026 with a 3 Oct federal deadline, now passed; advisory revised 2 Oct; exploiting actor not named
item.description: Cisco disclosed on 30 September that CVE-2026-76504, a flaw in how Catalyst SD-WAN Manager handles URI encoding, lets an unauthenticated remote attacker bypass an authentication rule protecting an API endpoint and gain administrator-level access. Cisco rates it CVSS 9.8, says it became aware of active exploitation in September without naming an actor, and lists no workarounds. CISA added it to KEV the same day with a 3 October federal deadline, now passed, and Cisco revised its advisory on 2 October. Fixed releases exist for each supported train; releases older than 20.9 must migrate. BleepingComputer counts it as the fifth SD-WAN zero-day exploited in 2026. In our assessment (editorial, not from the source), SD-WAN managers often control the WAN links that tie remote substations, plants and pipeline sites back to headquarters, so administrator takeover is a path toward those sites. - Cisco security advisory cisco-sa-sdwan-webauth-xr8beuuU; CISA KEV catalog; reported by BleepingComputer - Disclosed and added to KEV 30 Sep 2026; advisory revised 2 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] Fortinet confirms an exploited FortiMail zero-day, and its updated advisory now lists fixed releases
item.category: Advisory — Fortinet FortiMail path-traversal / NULL-byte zero-day (CVE-2026-104286, Fortinet CVSS 9.8) exploited in the wild; added to CISA KEV 1 Oct 2026 (deadline 4 Oct); Fortinet’s 5 Oct update lists fixed releases
item.description: Fortinet advisory FG-IR-26-175 describes a path-traversal and NULL-byte handling flaw that lets an unauthenticated attacker write arbitrary files on a FortiMail appliance through crafted HTTP or HTTPS requests. Fortinet scores it CVSS 9.8 and says it has been reported exploited in the wild; CISA added it to KEV on 1 October with a three-day federal deadline. Affected branches are 7.2, 7.4, 7.6 and 8.0. When the advisory first appeared the fixes were only planned, but Fortinet’s 5 October update lists fixed releases 7.4.9, 7.6.7 and 8.0.2, and tells 7.2 users to move to the 7.4 branch or later. In our assessment (editorial), FortiMail is an email gateway rather than an OT product, but it sits in the corporate trust zone that many plant networks inherit accounts and mail relays from, so a compromised gateway is a stepping stone worth closing off. - Fortinet PSIRT advisory FG-IR-26-175; CISA KEV catalog; reported by SecurityWeek - Disclosed and added to KEV 1 Oct 2026; fixed releases listed in Fortinet’s 5 Oct 2026 update

item.title: [Critical] SonicWall ships hotfixes for a maximum-severity flaw in SMA1000 remote-access gateways
item.category: Advisory — SonicWall rates CVE-2026-102255, a server-side request forgery in the SMA1000 Appliance WorkPlace interface, as maximum severity; unauthenticated, remote, low complexity; no exploitation reported; not in CISA KEV
item.description: SonicWall released hotfixes on 6 October for CVE-2026-102255, a server-side request forgery in the Appliance WorkPlace interface of SMA1000 gateways, which it rates as maximum severity. BleepingComputer reports the flaw can be reached remotely without authentication and with low complexity. It affects the SMA1000 6210, 7210 and 8200v models; the SMA100 series and SSL-VPN on SonicWall firewalls are not affected. SonicWall says it has no evidence of exploitation, and Shadowserver counts more than 400 internet-exposed SMA1000 appliances, some possibly already patched. The report gives no CVSS number or fixed version, so check the vendor advisory. Remote-access gateways like this are a common route for vendors and integrators into plant networks. - SonicWall advisory, reported by BleepingComputer; Shadowserver exposure data - Hotfixes released 6 Oct 2026; reported 7 Oct 2026

item.title: [Info] Industry coalition asks CISA for a binding directive on OT security inside federal agencies
item.category: Policy — OT Cybersecurity Coalition urges CISA to issue a binding operational directive on OT security at federal agencies; a proposal only, no CISA commitment; no CVE
item.description: The OT Cybersecurity Coalition is urging CISA to issue a Binding Operational Directive focused solely on operational technology at federal civilian agencies, CyberScoop reported on 6 October. The coalition wants each agency to name an accountable OT cybersecurity officer, meet minimum practices drawn from existing federal guidance and CISA’s 2022 Cybersecurity Performance Goals, and consider whether NSA’s OT guidance should apply to civilian agencies. It points to a 30 September GAO report finding that only 7 of 22 civilian agencies fully met OMB’s requirements for networked IoT and OT devices, and to this summer’s water-utility attacks. CISA did not respond to CyberScoop and has announced no directive. In our assessment, a directive would bind only federal agencies but would signal what CISA expects of OT programs generally. - OT Cybersecurity Coalition paper, reported by CyberScoop; GAO-26-108937 - Reported 6 Oct 2026; GAO report 30 Sep 2026

item.title: [Info] FBI and CISA: your ICS integrator’s access to your plant is your risk too, not just theirs
item.category: Guidance — FBI/CISA fact sheet on third-party ICS integrator risk, prompted by a prior compromise of a US industrial automation/SCADA integrator; no CVE, no new confirmed operator intrusion
item.description: The FBI and CISA published a joint fact sheet on third-party ICS integrator risk on 24 September, prompted by a prior compromise of a US industrial automation company that provided system integration, engineering consulting and SCADA programming. The agencies say intruders searched the company’s systems for terms like “customers” and “SCADA” and staged customer SCADA information, ICS device details and schematics for exfiltration; downstream customers referenced in the guidance include power utilities and transportation entities. The guidance recommends least-privilege integrator access, on-demand and auditable remote sessions, a full inventory of supplied hardware and software, security terms in contracts, and the ability to operate manually if an integrator is compromised. - FBI and CISA joint fact sheet; reported by Industrial Cyber - Released 24 Sep 2026
